```{r}
dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
# Chemin relatif : Quarto embarque les PNG dans le HTML et les écrit aussi sur disque.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.path = "sorties/figures/",
  dev = "png",
  dpi = 200

# Sankey (htmlwidget) : PNG disque si webshot2 est disponible
save_widget_png <- function(widget, filename, width = 900, height = 500) {
  png_path <- file.path(fig_dir, paste0(filename, ".png"))
  if (!requireNamespace("htmlwidgets", quietly = TRUE)) {
    warning("htmlwidgets manquant : PNG Sankey non écrit.")
    return(invisible(png_path))
  }
  tmp_html <- tempfile(fileext = ".html")
  on.exit(unlink(tmp_html), add = TRUE)
  htmlwidgets::saveWidget(widget, tmp_html, selfcontained = TRUE)
  if (requireNamespace("webshot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
    tryCatch(
      webshot2::webshot(tmp_html, png_path, vwidth = width, vheight = height, zoom = 2),
      error = function(e) warning("Sankey HTML seulement (webshot2 : ", e$message, ")")
    )
  } else {
    warning("Installe webshot2 pour exporter les Sankey en PNG dans sorties/figures/.")
  }
  invisible(png_path)
}
```

### a. Weanlings

```{r}
#| label: fig-sankey-calves
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
library(networkD3)

sankey_calves_ref_pct <- function(res){
  ivv_days <- res$breakdown$IVV
  mo_y     <- res$breakdown$MO_WEAN
  tr_eff   <- res$breakdown$TR_eff_ref
  B <- 365 / ivv_days
  died_share     <- mo_y
  survived_share <- 1 - mo_y
  renew_share    <- tr_eff / B
  sold_share     <- max(survived_share - renew_share, 0)

  pct  <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
  valp <- function(x) round(100 * x, 1)
  nodes <- data.frame(name = c(
    "Calves born (100%)",
    paste0("Died pre-weaning (", pct(died_share), ")"),
    paste0("Survived (",       pct(survived_share), ")"),
    paste0("Renewal (",        pct(renew_share), ")"),
    paste0("Sold (",           pct(sold_share), ")")
  ))
  links <- data.frame(
    source = c(0, 0, 2, 2),
    target = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
    value  = c(valp(died_share), valp(survived_share), valp(renew_share), valp(sold_share))
  )
  sankeyNetwork(
    Links = links, Nodes = nodes,
    Source = "source", Target = "target", Value = "value", NodeID = "name",
    fontSize = 12, nodeWidth = 24, sinksRight = TRUE
  )
}

p_sankey_calves <- sankey_calves_ref_pct(res_ref)
save_widget_png(p_sankey_calves, "fig-sankey-calves")
p_sankey_calves
```

### b. Cows

```{r}
#| label: fig-sankey-cows
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
library(networkD3)

sankey_ref_pct <- function(res){
  mo  <- res$breakdown$MO_COW
  cu  <- res$breakdown$CULL_used
  tr  <- res$breakdown$TR_eff_ref

  if (is.null(mo) || is.null(cu) || is.null(tr))
    stop("Certains éléments nécessaires (MO_COW, CULL_used, TR_eff_ref) manquent dans res$breakdown")

  rest <- 1 - tr
  repl <- tr
  pct  <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
  valp <- function(x) round(100 * x, 1)

  nodes <- data.frame(
    name = c(
      "COWS_t",
      paste0("Mortality (", pct(mo), ")"),
      paste0("Culling (",   pct(cu), ")"),
      paste0("Remain (",    pct(rest), ")"),
      paste0("Replacements (", pct(repl), ")"),
      "COWS_t+1"
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  links <- data.frame(
    source = c(0, 0, 0, 4, 3),
    target = c(1, 2, 3, 5, 5),
    value  = c(valp(mo), valp(cu), valp(rest), valp(repl), valp(rest))
  )

  sankeyNetwork(
    Links = links, Nodes = nodes,
    Source = "source", Target = "target", Value = "value", NodeID = "name",
    fontSize = 12, nodeWidth = 24, sinksRight = TRUE
  )
}

p_sankey_cows <- sankey_ref_pct(res_ref)
save_widget_png(p_sankey_cows, "fig-sankey-cows")
p_sankey_cows
```

## 3. Stochastic simulation

### a. parameters

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(knitr)
library(here)

#désactiver affichage scientifique des valeurs
options(scipen = 999)


# 1) Charger le CSV des distributions
dist_tbl <- read.csv(here::here("config/stochastic_2023_2.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# 2) Harmoniser les noms de colonnes (si ton CSV utilise d'autres noms)
#    -> on essaye de retrouver automatiquement les colonnes usuelles
nm <- names(dist_tbl)

col_param <- intersect(nm, c("param", "Parameter", "name", "Name"))[1]
col_dist  <- intersect(nm, c("dist", "Dist", "distribution", "Distribution"))[1]
col_mean  <- intersect(nm, c("mean", "Mean", "mu"))[1]
col_sd    <- intersect(nm, c("sd", "SD", "sigma"))[1]
col_min   <- intersect(nm, c("min", "Min", "lower", "Lower"))[1]
col_max   <- intersect(nm, c("max", "Max", "upper", "Upper"))[1]

# Sécurité : si certaines colonnes n'existent pas, on les crée à NA
if (is.na(col_param)) stop("Colonne 'param' introuvable dans dist_tbl.")
if (is.na(col_dist))  stop("Colonne 'dist' (distribution) introuvable dans dist_tbl.")

dist_clean <- dist_tbl %>%
  transmute(
    Parameter    = .data[[col_param]],
    Distribution = .data[[col_dist]],
    Mean         = if (!is.na(col_mean)) .data[[col_mean]] else NA_real_,
    SD           = if (!is.na(col_sd))   .data[[col_sd]]   else NA_real_,
    Min          = if (!is.na(col_min))  .data[[col_min]]  else NA_real_,
    Max          = if (!is.na(col_max))  .data[[col_max]]  else NA_real_
  )

# 3) Dictionnaire (params_stoch2) : descriptions lisibles
params_stoch2 <- tibble::tibble(
  Parameter = c(
    "MO_COW", "MO_WEAN", "CULL", "IVV",
    "PRICE_CULL", "PRICE_WEANM", "PRICE_WEANF"
  ),
  Description = c(
    "Adult female mortality rate",
    "Calf mortality rate",
    "Culling rate",
    "Calving interval (days)",
    "Cull cow sale price (€)",
    "Weanling male sale price (€)",
    "Weanling heifer sale price (€)"
  )
)

# 4) Joindre les descriptions
stoch_tbl <- dist_clean %>%
  left_join(params_stoch2, by = "Parameter") %>%
  relocate(Description, .after = Parameter) %>%
  arrange(Parameter)

# 5) Afficher dans le Quarto
knitr::kable(
  stoch_tbl,
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Baseline stochastic input parameters and probability distributions used in the Monte Carlo simulations",
  col.names = c("Parameter", "Description", "Distribution", "Mean", "SD", "Min", "Max")
)

```

### b. Gross Margins (EHD-free, HED, delta)

\
Distribution des marges brutes et écart entre scénario (référence, mhe) suivant des jeux de données tirés aléatoirement, dans des distributions normales bornées, de valeurs des paramètres d'élevage (taux d'abattage, mortalité vache et veau, IVV) et des prix de vente (vache et broutard mâles et femelles).

```{r}
#| label: stochastic
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)

# --- 1) Charger les paramètres de distributions ---
dist_tbl <- read.csv(here::here("config/stochastic_2023_2.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# --- 2) Sampler-----
rnorm_clamp <- function(mean, sd, minv = -Inf, maxv = Inf) {
  x <- rnorm(1, mean, sd)
  x <- max(min(x, maxv), minv)
  x
}

# bornes par défaut
param_bounds <- function(name) {
  switch(name,
    "CULL"    = c(0, 1),
    "MO_COW" = c(0, 1),
    "MO_WEAN"  = c(0, 1),
    "IVV"      = c(250, 520),     #  pour éviter valeurs absurdes
    # prix et coûts : bornes larges
    "PRICE_CULL"= c(0, Inf),
    "PRICE_WEANM"= c(0, Inf),
   "PRICE_WEANF"= c(0, Inf),
    c(-Inf, Inf)
  )
}

draw_params_once <- function(base_params, dist_tbl) {
  p <- base_params
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(dist_tbl))) {
    nm   <- dist_tbl$param[i]
    dist <- dist_tbl$dist[i]
    mu   <- dist_tbl$mean[i]
    sd   <- dist_tbl$sd[i]
    rng  <- param_bounds(nm)

    val <- switch(dist,
      "normal" = rnorm_clamp(mu, sd, rng[1], rng[2]),
      stop(sprintf("Distribution '%s' non gérée pour %s", dist, nm))
    )

    p[[nm]] <- val
  }
  p
}

# --- 3) Monte Carlo autour de la référence ---
run_mc <- function(B = 1000, seed = 123) {
  set.seed(seed)
  out <- vector("list", B)

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    # 3.1 Tirer un jeu de paramètres
    p_ref <- draw_params_once(params_eco, dist_tbl)

    # 3.2 calcul du TR_eff_ref = CULL + MO_COW du TIRAGE*
    TR_eff_ref_row <- p_ref$CULL + p_ref$MO_COW

    # 3.3 Scénario REF
    res_ref <- run_scenario(p_ref, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = FALSE)

    # 3.4 Scénario MHE (impacts constants ; TR_eff_ref_row inchangé)*
    p_mhe <- apply_impacts(p_ref, impacts_mhe)
    p_mhe$COST_VET_D <- 15
    p_mhe <- apply_mhe_restr(p_mhe, restr = restr_on)
    res_mhe <- run_scenario(p_mhe, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = TRUE)

    out[[b]] <- data.frame(
      draw = b,
      MB_ref = res_ref$MB_op,
      MB_mhe = res_mhe$MB_op,
      dMB    = res_mhe$MB_op - res_ref$MB_op
    )
  }

  do.call(rbind, out)
}

# --- 4) Lancer, résumer, visualiser ---
mc_res <- run_mc(B = 2000, seed = 42)

# Résumé statistique
summ <- within(data.frame(
  mean_MB_ref = mean(mc_res$MB_ref),
  sd_MB_ref   = sd(mc_res$MB_ref),
  mean_MB_mhe = mean(mc_res$MB_mhe),
  sd_MB_mhe   = sd(mc_res$MB_mhe),
  mean_dMB    = mean(mc_res$dMB),
  sd_dMB      = sd(mc_res$dMB),
  q025_dMB     = quantile(mc_res$dMB, 0.025),
  q50_dMB     = quantile(mc_res$dMB, 0.50),
  q975_dMB     = quantile(mc_res$dMB, 0.975),
  p_dMB_neg   = mean(mc_res$dMB < 0)
), {})


kable(summ)


#| label: sim_interval_normal
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(dplyr)
library(knitr)



```

### c. Decomposition

```{r}
#| label: stochastic_decompos
#| warning: false


# --- 1) Charger les paramètres de distributions ---
dist_tbl <- read.csv(here::here("config/stochastic_2023_2.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# --- 2) Sampler-----
rnorm_clamp <- function(mean, sd, minv = -Inf, maxv = Inf) {
  x <- rnorm(1, mean, sd)
  x <- max(min(x, maxv), minv)
  x
}

# bornes par défaut
param_bounds <- function(name) {
  switch(name,
    "CULL"    = c(0, 1),
    "MO_COW" = c(0, 1),
    "MO_WEAN"  = c(0, 1),
    "IVV"      = c(250, 520),     #  pour éviter valeurs absurdes
    # prix et coûts : bornes larges
    "PRICE_CULL"= c(0, Inf),
    "PRICE_WEANM"= c(0, Inf),
   "PRICE_WEANF"= c(0, Inf),
    c(-Inf, Inf)
  )
}

draw_params_once <- function(base_params, dist_tbl) {
  p <- base_params
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(dist_tbl))) {
    nm   <- dist_tbl$param[i]
    dist <- dist_tbl$dist[i]
    mu   <- dist_tbl$mean[i]
    sd   <- dist_tbl$sd[i]
    rng  <- param_bounds(nm)

    val <- switch(dist,
      "normal" = rnorm_clamp(mu, sd, rng[1], rng[2]),
      stop(sprintf("Distribution '%s' non gérée pour %s", dist, nm))
    )

    p[[nm]] <- val
  }
  p
}


# --- Helper : récupérer REV_WEAN total même si m/f sont séparés ---
get_REV_WEAN <- function(bd) {
  if (!is.null(bd$REV_WEAN)) {
    bd$REV_WEAN
  } else if (!is.null(bd$REV_WEAN_m) && !is.null(bd$REV_WEAN_f)) {
    bd$REV_WEAN_m + bd$REV_WEAN_f
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }
}

# --- Monte Carlo avec décomposition complète (REF & MHE) ---
run_mc_decomp <- function(B = 2000, seed = 42) {
  set.seed(seed)
  out <- vector("list", B)

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    # 1) Tirage de paramètres autour de la référence
    p_ref <- draw_params_once(params_eco, dist_tbl)

    # 2) TR_eff_ref du tirage (règle v03)
    TR_eff_ref_row <- p_ref$CULL + p_ref$MO_COW

    # 3) Scénario REF
    res_ref <- run_scenario(p_ref, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = FALSE)

    # 4) Scénario MHE : impacts constants (tes 'impacts_mhe') + surcoûts
    p_mhe <- apply_impacts(p_ref, impacts_mhe)
    p_mhe$COST_VET_D <- 15
    p_mhe <- apply_mhe_restr(p_mhe, restr = restr_on)
    res_mhe <- run_scenario(p_mhe, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = TRUE)

    # 5) Empiler la décomposition pour REF et MHE
    out[[b]] <- rbind(
      data.frame(
        draw = b, scen = "REF",
        REV_COW     = res_ref$breakdown$REV_COW,
        REV_WEAN      = get_REV_WEAN(res_ref$breakdown),
        COST_PROD  = res_ref$breakdown$COST_PROD,
        COST_VET_D = res_ref$breakdown$COST_VET_D,
        COST_PRIX  = res_ref$breakdown$COST_PRIX,
        COST_BLOC  = res_ref$breakdown$COST_BLOC,
        COST_PCR   = res_ref$breakdown$COST_PCR,
        COST_RESTR = res_ref$breakdown$COST_RESTR,
        n_WEAN_sold = res_ref$breakdown$n_WEAN_sold,
        MB_op      = res_ref$MB_op,
        check.names = FALSE
      ),
      data.frame(
        draw = b, scen = "MHE",
        REV_COW     = res_mhe$breakdown$REV_COW,
        REV_WEAN      = get_REV_WEAN(res_mhe$breakdown),
        COST_PROD  = res_mhe$breakdown$COST_PROD,
        COST_VET_D = res_mhe$breakdown$COST_VET_D,
        COST_PRIX  = res_mhe$breakdown$COST_PRIX,
        COST_BLOC  = res_mhe$breakdown$COST_BLOC,
        COST_PCR   = res_mhe$breakdown$COST_PCR,
        COST_RESTR = res_mhe$breakdown$COST_RESTR,
        n_WEAN_sold = res_mhe$breakdown$n_WEAN_sold,
        MB_op      = res_mhe$MB_op,
        check.names = FALSE
      )
    )
  }

  dplyr::bind_rows(out)
}

# --- Lancer et calculer les MOYENNES par scénario ---
mc_decomp <- run_mc_decomp(B = 2000, seed = 42)

moyennes_stoch <- mc_decomp %>%
  dplyr::group_by(scen) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    REV_COW     = mean(REV_COW,     na.rm = TRUE),
    REV_WEAN      = mean(REV_WEAN,      na.rm = TRUE),
    COST_PROD  = mean(COST_PROD,  na.rm = TRUE),
    COST_VET_D = mean(COST_VET_D, na.rm = TRUE),
    COST_PRIX  = mean(COST_PRIX,  na.rm = TRUE),
    COST_BLOC  = mean(COST_BLOC,  na.rm = TRUE),
    COST_PCR   = mean(COST_PCR,   na.rm = TRUE),
    COST_RESTR = mean(COST_RESTR, na.rm = TRUE),
    MB_op      = mean(MB_op,      na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

moyennes_stoch
```

### definition of ehd_only_cost_steps

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

ehd_only_cost_steps <- c("COST_VET_D", "COST_RESTR")

prep_mc_long_stoch <- function(dat, restr) {
  decomp_cols <- if (isTRUE(restr)) {
    c("REV_COW", "REV_WEAN", "COST_VET_D", "COST_RESTR", "MB_op")
  } else {
    c("REV_COW", "REV_WEAN", "MB_op")
  }
  step_levels <- decomp_cols
  step_labels <- c(
    REV_COW     = "Culled cows",
    REV_WEAN    = "Weanlings",
    COST_VET_D  = "Treatments",
    COST_RESTR  = "Restrictions",
    MB_op       = ""
  )[step_levels]
  mc_long <- dat %>%
    mutate(scenario = recode(scen, "REF" = "EHD-free", "MHE" = "EHD")) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = all_of(decomp_cols),
      names_to = "step",
      values_to = "value"
    ) %>%
    filter(!(step %in% ehd_only_cost_steps & scenario == "EHD-free")) %>%
    mutate(
      type = case_when(
        step %in% c("REV_COW", "REV_WEAN") ~ "PRODUCTS (sales)",
        step %in% ehd_only_cost_steps      ~ "COSTS",
        TRUE                               ~ "GROSS MARGIN"
      ),
      type = factor(
        type,
        levels = if (isTRUE(restr)) {
          c("PRODUCTS (sales)", "COSTS", "GROSS MARGIN")
        } else {
          c("PRODUCTS (sales)", "GROSS MARGIN")
        }
      ),
      scenario = factor(scenario, levels = c("EHD-free", "EHD")),
      step = factor(step, levels = step_levels, labels = step_labels)
    )
  list(mc_long = mc_long, step_levels = step_levels, step_labels = step_labels)
}
```

## 5. Costs, revenues and annual gross margin per cow in the EHD scenario compared with the EHD-free scenario.

Costs include veterinary treatments and sanitary and commercial restrictions (PCR testing, additional animal retention and reduced sale prices).

```{r}
#| label: graph_stoch_en_bl2
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| cache: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# --- 1) Long format (même règle que graph_stoch_en_bl) ---
stoch_vis <- prep_mc_long_stoch(mc_decomp, restr_on)
mc_long <- stoch_vis$mc_long

# --- 3) Pré-calcul des stats (moyenne + "IC ~ 95%" = mean ± 1.96*sd) ---
sum_df <- mc_long %>%
  group_by(type, step, scenario) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd   = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ymin  = mean - 1.96 * sd,
    ymax  = mean + 1.96 * sd,
    label_y = mean + 135 + ifelse(scenario == "EHD-free", 55, 0),
    label = paste0("€", format(round(mean, 0), big.mark = ",", decimal.mark = "."))
  )

# Largeur de barre fixe (unités x). Les groupes à 1 barre (EHD-only) sont
# collés avec le même écart que EHD-free / EHD, sans réserver un second slot.
bar_w     <- 0.72
pair_gap  <- 0.12
group_gap <- 0.50
type_origin <- c(
  "PRODUCTS (sales)" = 0,
  "COSTS"            = 100,
  "GROSS MARGIN"     = 200
)

place_bars <- function(df) {
  steps <- if (is.factor(df$step)) {
    intersect(levels(droplevels(df$step)), as.character(df$step))
  } else {
    unique(as.character(df$step))
  }
  origin <- unname(type_origin[as.character(df$type[1])])
  cursor <- origin
  rows <- list()
  for (st in steps) {
    sl <- df[df$step == st, , drop = FALSE]
    sl <- sl[order(sl$scenario), , drop = FALSE]
    n <- nrow(sl)
    if (n == 2) {
      sl$x <- c(cursor + bar_w / 2, cursor + bar_w + pair_gap + bar_w / 2)
      width_this <- 2 * bar_w + pair_gap
      next_gap <- group_gap
    } else {
      sl$x <- cursor + bar_w / 2
      width_this <- bar_w
      next_gap <- pair_gap
    }
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- sl
    cursor <- cursor + width_this + next_gap
  }
  bind_rows(rows)
}

sum_df <- bind_rows(lapply(split(sum_df, sum_df$type, drop = TRUE), place_bars))
axis_df <- bind_rows(lapply(split(sum_df, sum_df$type, drop = TRUE), function(d) {
  steps <- if (is.factor(d$step)) {
    intersect(levels(droplevels(d$step)), as.character(d$step))
  } else {
    unique(as.character(d$step))
  }
  data.frame(
    x = unname(vapply(steps, function(st) mean(d$x[as.character(d$step) == st]), numeric(1))),
    lab = steps,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))
axis_df <- axis_df[nzchar(axis_df$lab), , drop = FALSE]

# --- 4) Graphique : space=free_x proportionnel à l'emprise réelle des barres ---
ggplot(sum_df, aes(x = x, y = mean, fill = scenario)) +
  geom_col(width = bar_w) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), width = 0.12) +
  geom_label(
    aes(y = label_y, label = label),
    size = 3.2,
    color = "black",
    fill  = "white",
    label.size = 0,
    label.padding = unit(0.12, "lines")
  ) +
  facet_grid(. ~ type, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x", switch = "x") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4, color = "grey30") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = axis_df$x,
    labels = axis_df$lab,
    expand = expansion(add = 0.15)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(
      accuracy = 1,
      big.mark = ",",
      decimal.mark = ".",
      prefix = "€"
    ),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.15))
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "€/cow/year", fill = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("EHD-free" = "grey20", "EHD" = "grey70"),
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    legend.position    = "bottom",
    strip.placement    = "outside",
    axis.text.x        = element_text(size = 10)
  )
```

## 6.Decomposition of EHD-associated economic losses

Points represent mean losses for each component and the total gross margin loss. Horizontal error bars indicate the central 95% simulation intervals (2.5th–97.5th percentiles) from 2,000 Monte Carlo iterations. Treatment and restriction-related costs are shown without intervals; uncertainty in restriction-related costs was explored separately through deterministic sensitivity analyses.

```{r}

#| label: graph_stoch_delta
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| cache: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# --- 1. Apparier les scénarios par itération ---

# IMPORTANT : suppose que REF et MHE ont le même ordre
# de tirage. Si un identifiant d'itération existe,
# l'utiliser à la place de row_number().

mc_paired <- mc_decomp %>%
  group_by(scen) %>%
  mutate(iter = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

stopifnot(
  sum(mc_paired$scen == "REF") ==
    sum(mc_paired$scen == "MHE")
)

mc_wide <- mc_paired %>%
  select(iter, scen, REV_COW, REV_WEAN,
         COST_VET_D, COST_RESTR, MB_op) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = iter,
    names_from = scen,
    values_from = c(REV_COW, REV_WEAN,
                    COST_VET_D, COST_RESTR, MB_op)
  )

# --- 2. Calcul des pertes par itération ---

mc_losses <- mc_wide %>%
  transmute(
    iter,
    `Culled cows` = REV_COW_REF - REV_COW_MHE,
    `Weanlings` = REV_WEAN_REF - REV_WEAN_MHE,
    `Treatments` = COST_VET_D_MHE,
    `Restrictions` = if (isTRUE(restr_on)) {
      COST_RESTR_MHE
    } else {
      0
    },
    `Total gross margin loss` = MB_op_REF - MB_op_MHE
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -iter,
    names_to = "component",
    values_to = "loss"
  )

# --- 3. Moyennes et intervalles de simulation ---

summary_losses <- mc_losses %>%
  group_by(component) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(loss, na.rm = TRUE),
    lower = quantile(loss, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    upper = quantile(loss, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Pas d'intervalle affiché pour ces deux postes
    show_interval = !component %in%
      c("Treatments", "Restrictions"),

    # Ordre d'affichage, du haut vers le bas
    component = factor(
      component,
      levels = rev(c(
        "Weanlings",
        "Culled cows",
        "Treatments",
        "Restrictions",
        "Total gross margin loss"
      ))
    ),

    # Affichage des valeurs moyennes
    label = paste0("€", round(mean, 0))
  )

if (!isTRUE(restr_on)) {
  summary_losses <- summary_losses %>%
    filter(component != "Restrictions")
}

# --- 4. Graphique ---

# Espace à droite des intervalles pour les étiquettes
x_max <- max(
  summary_losses$upper[summary_losses$show_interval],
  na.rm = TRUE
)

offset <- x_max * 0.035

ggplot(summary_losses, aes(y = component, x = mean)) +

  # Intervalles centraux à 95 %
  geom_segment(
    data = filter(summary_losses, show_interval),
    aes(x = lower, xend = upper,
        y = component, yend = component),
    linewidth = 0.65,
    color = "grey30"
  ) +

  # Extrémités des intervalles
  geom_errorbar(
    data = filter(summary_losses, show_interval),
    aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper),
    width = 0.15,
    linewidth = 0.65,
    color = "grey30",
    orientation = "y"
  ) +

  # Estimations moyennes
  geom_point(
    aes(shape = show_interval),
    size = 3,
    color = "grey20"
  ) +

  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("TRUE" = 16, "FALSE" = 15),
    guide = "none"
  ) +

  # Valeurs moyennes inscrites à côté des points
  geom_text(
    aes(
      x = ifelse(show_interval, upper, mean) + offset,
      label = label
    ),
    hjust = 0,
    size = 3.5,
    color = "grey20"
  ) +

  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linewidth = 0.4,
    color = "grey30"
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = label_number(
      accuracy = 1,
      big.mark = ",",
      prefix = "€"
    ),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.20))
  ) +

  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(0, x_max + 4 * offset),
    clip = "off"
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "EHD-associated loss (€/cow/year)",
    y = NULL
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(
      color = "grey90",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      color = "grey30",
      size = 11
    ),
    axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey40"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(
      color = "black",
      margin = margin(t = 12)
    ),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.margin = margin(10, 35, 10, 10)
  )

# Contrôle des valeurs
print(summary_losses)
```

## 8. 4 Scenarii simulation

### a. Scenarii definition

```{r}
#| warning: false

## --- Impacts MHE : low vs high ---------------------------------

# Impacts additifs (excess) appliqués au scénario EHD :
# - adult female mortality: +1 pp
# - calf mortality: +2 pp
# - calving interval: +10 days

impacts_none <- NULL  # pour le scénario EHD-free

impacts_init <- list(
  dMO_COW = 0.01,  # +1 pp
  dMO_WEAN  = 0.02,  # +2 pp
  dIVV      = 10     # +10 days
)

# Low severity: impacts /2 (tous les paramètres d'impact à la fois)
impacts_low <- list(
  dMO_COW = impacts_init$dMO_COW / 2,  # 0.005
  dMO_WEAN  = impacts_init$dMO_WEAN  / 2,  # 0.01
  dIVV      = impacts_init$dIVV      / 2   # 5
)

# High severity: impacts ×2 (tous les paramètres d'impact à la fois)
impacts_high <- list(
  dMO_COW = impacts_init$dMO_COW * 2,  # 0.02
  dMO_WEAN  = impacts_init$dMO_WEAN  * 2,  # 0.04
  dIVV      = impacts_init$dIVV      * 2   # 20
)

# définition 5 scénarios (EHD-free + 4 configurations)
library(tibble)

scenarios <- tribble(
  ~scenario,                 ~impact_level, ~weanling_price,
  "EHD_free",                "none",        1400,
  "Low_EHD_low_price",       "low",         1100,
  "Low_EHD_high_price",      "low",         1700,
  "High_EHD_low_price",      "high",        1100,
  "High_EHD_high_price",     "high",        1700
)



#utilitaires :
# Appliquer un prix de broutard à JM et JF
apply_weanling_price <- function(p, price) {
  p$PRICE_WEANM <- price
  p$PRICE_WEANF <- price
  p
}

# Récupérer l'objet d'impacts en fonction du niveau
get_impacts_obj <- function(level) {
  switch(level,
    "none" = impacts_none,
    "low"  = impacts_low,
    "high" = impacts_high,
    stop("Niveau d'impact inconnu : ", level)
  )
}


#MC par scenario

run_mc_one_scenario <- function(scen_row, B = 2000, seed = 42) {
  set.seed(seed)
  out <- vector("list", B)

  impacts_obj <- get_impacts_obj(scen_row$impact_level)
  is_ehd_free <- identical(scen_row$impact_level, "none")

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {

    p_ref <- draw_params_once(params_eco, dist_tbl)

    p_ref <- apply_weanling_price(p_ref, scen_row$weanling_price)

    TR_eff_ref_row <- p_ref$CULL + p_ref$MO_COW

    res_ref <- run_scenario(p_ref, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = FALSE)

    if (is_ehd_free) {
      res_mhe_MB <- res_ref$MB_op
    } else {
      p_mhe <- apply_impacts(p_ref, impacts_obj)
      p_mhe$COST_VET_D <- 15
      p_mhe <- apply_mhe_restr(p_mhe, restr = restr_on)
      res_mhe <- run_scenario(p_mhe, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = TRUE)
      res_mhe_MB <- res_mhe$MB_op
    }

    out[[b]] <- data.frame(
      draw   = b,
      MB_ref = res_ref$MB_op,
      MB_mhe = res_mhe_MB,
      dMB    = res_mhe_MB - res_ref$MB_op
    )
  }

  mc_tmp <- do.call(rbind, out)

  data.frame(
    scenario    = scen_row$scenario,
    mean_MB_ref = mean(mc_tmp$MB_ref),
    sd_MB_ref   = sd(mc_tmp$MB_ref),
    mean_MB_mhe = mean(mc_tmp$MB_mhe),
    sd_MB_mhe   = sd(mc_tmp$MB_mhe),
    mean_dMB    = mean(mc_tmp$dMB),
    sd_dMB      = sd(mc_tmp$dMB),
    q05_dMB     = quantile(mc_tmp$dMB, 0.05),
    q50_dMB     = quantile(mc_tmp$dMB, 0.50),
    q95_dMB     = quantile(mc_tmp$dMB, 0.95),
    p_dMB_neg   = mean(mc_tmp$dMB < 0)
  )
}


library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

res_scenarios <- scenarios %>%
  group_split(scenario) %>%
  lapply(\(df) run_mc_one_scenario(df[1, ], B = 2000, seed = 42)) %>%
  bind_rows()




```

## 9. One-way sensitivity tornado diagram for gross-margin loss

Bars show the change in gross-margin loss obtained by setting each EHD-impact parameter to its lower and upper bound. The vertical dashed line represents the mean loss from the reference comparison. All parameters decrease gross margin (negative effect).

Parameter bounds used in the analysis were: excess adult female mortality 0–3 pp; excess calf mortality 0–6 pp; and increase in calving interval 0–30 days.

```{r}
#| label: fig-tornado
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
## Scénario d'impact MHE "initial"
impacts_init <- list(
  dMO_COW = 0.01,
  dMO_WEAN  = 0.02,
  dIVV      = 10
)

## Plages low/high : low = 0 (pas d'impact), high = 2×impact initial
range_impacts <- list(
  dMO_COW = c(low = 0, high = 3 * impacts_init$dMO_COW),
  dMO_WEAN  = c(low = 0, high = 3 * impacts_init$dMO_WEAN),
  dIVV      = c(low = 0, high = 3 * impacts_init$dIVV)
)

## Scénarios "un paramètre à la fois" + scénario initial
impact_scenarios <- list(
  "init"     = impacts_init,

  "AF_low"   = list(
    dMO_COW = range_impacts$dMO_COW[["low"]],
    dMO_WEAN  = impacts_init$dMO_WEAN,
    dIVV      = impacts_init$dIVV
  ),
  "AF_high"  = list(
    dMO_COW = range_impacts$dMO_COW[["high"]],
    dMO_WEAN  = impacts_init$dMO_WEAN,
    dIVV      = impacts_init$dIVV
  ),

  "Y_low"    = list(
    dMO_COW = impacts_init$dMO_COW,
    dMO_WEAN  = range_impacts$dMO_WEAN[["low"]],
    dIVV      = impacts_init$dIVV
  ),
  "Y_high"   = list(
    dMO_COW = impacts_init$dMO_COW,
    dMO_WEAN  = range_impacts$dMO_WEAN[["high"]],
    dIVV      = impacts_init$dIVV
  ),

  "IVV_low"  = list(
    dMO_COW = impacts_init$dMO_COW,
    dMO_WEAN  = impacts_init$dMO_WEAN,
    dIVV      = range_impacts$dIVV[["low"]]
  ),
  "IVV_high" = list(
    dMO_COW = impacts_init$dMO_COW,
    dMO_WEAN  = impacts_init$dMO_WEAN,
    dIVV      = range_impacts$dIVV[["high"]]
  )
)


run_mc_for_impacts <- function(impacts_obj, label = "scenario", B = 2000, seed = 42) {
  set.seed(seed)
  out <- vector("list", B)

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    # 1) Tirage des paramètres de base (sans MHE)
    p_ref <- draw_params_once(params_eco, dist_tbl)

    # 2) Calcul de l'efficacité de reproduction de référence
    TR_eff_ref_row <- p_ref$CULL + p_ref$MO_COW

    # 3) Scénario de référence sans MHE
    res_ref <- run_scenario(p_ref, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = FALSE)

    # 4) Scénario avec MHE (impacts_obj = dMO_COW, dMO_WEAN, dIVV)
    p_mhe <- apply_impacts(p_ref, impacts_obj)
    p_mhe$COST_VET_D <- 15
    p_mhe <- apply_mhe_restr(p_mhe, restr = restr_on)

    res_mhe <- run_scenario(p_mhe, TR_eff_ref_row, mhe = TRUE)

    out[[b]] <- data.frame(
      draw   = b,
      MB_ref = res_ref$MB_op,
      MB_mhe = res_mhe$MB_op,
      dMB    = res_mhe$MB_op - res_ref$MB_op
    )
  }

  mc_tmp <- do.call(rbind, out)

  data.frame(
    impact_scenario = label,
    mean_MB_ref = mean(mc_tmp$MB_ref),
    sd_MB_ref   = sd(mc_tmp$MB_ref),
    mean_MB_mhe = mean(mc_tmp$MB_mhe),
    sd_MB_mhe   = sd(mc_tmp$MB_mhe),
    mean_dMB    = mean(mc_tmp$dMB),
    sd_dMB      = sd(mc_tmp$dMB),
    q05_dMB     = quantile(mc_tmp$dMB, 0.05),
    q50_dMB     = quantile(mc_tmp$dMB, 0.50),
    q95_dMB     = quantile(mc_tmp$dMB, 0.95),
    p_dMB_neg   = mean(mc_tmp$dMB < 0)
  )
}


library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

res_impacts <- lapply(names(impact_scenarios), function(nm) {
  run_mc_for_impacts(
    impacts_obj = impact_scenarios[[nm]],
    label       = nm,
    B           = 2000,
    seed        = 42
  )
}) %>%
  bind_rows()

kable(res_impacts, digits = 2)


#===========================TORNADO========================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# --- 1) baseline : scénario "init" ---------------------------------
base_dMB <- res_impacts %>%
  filter(impact_scenario == "init") %>%
  pull(mean_dMB)

# --- 2) Correspondance paramètre <-> scénarios low/high -----------
sens_structure <- tibble::tibble(
  impact     = c("dMO_COW", "dMO_WEAN", "dIVV"),
  scen_low   = c("AF_low",    "Y_low",    "IVV_low"),
  scen_high  = c("AF_high",   "Y_high",   "IVV_high")
)

# --- 3) torn : Récupérer les dMB low / high pour chaque paramètre --------
torn_df <- sens_structure %>%
  left_join(
    res_impacts %>% select(impact_scenario, mean_dMB),
    by = c("scen_low" = "impact_scenario")
  ) %>%
  rename(dMB_low = mean_dMB) %>%
  left_join(
    res_impacts %>% select(impact_scenario, mean_dMB),
    by = c("scen_high" = "impact_scenario")
  ) %>%
  rename(dMB_high = mean_dMB) %>%
  mutate(
    min_val = pmin(dMB_low, dMB_high),
    max_val = pmax(dMB_low, dMB_high),
    from    = min_val,
    to      = max_val
  )


# --- 4) Dictionnaire d'étiquettes lisibles ------------------------
labels_map <- c(
  dMO_COW = "Cow mortality rate",
  dMO_WEAN  = "Calf mortality rate",
  dIVV      = "Calving interval"
)

torn_df$impact_label <- labels_map[torn_df$impact]

# Option : trier par importance de l'amplitude (comme ton code)
torn_df <- torn_df %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(to - from)))

# --- 5) Graphique tornado -----------------------------------------
ggplot(torn_df,
       aes(y = reorder(impact_label, abs(to - from)))) +
  # barre principale (du min au max, en valeur de perte brute)
  geom_segment(aes(x = from, xend = to, yend = impact_label),
               linewidth = 6, lineend = "round") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = round(base_dMB, 0), linetype = 2) +
  labs(
    title    = "Sensitivity of gross margin loss to EHD impacts",
    subtitle = paste0("One-way sensitivity (dashed line = mean loss = ",
                      round(base_dMB, 0), " €/cow/year)"),
    x        = "Gross margin loss (€/cow/year)",   # 👈 ici
    y        = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x       = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y        = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.title         = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")
  )


```
